proposals.evidence: DEDR707 gives Malayalam uṟaṅṅuka sleep, Kannada oṟagu/oṟaṅgu and Kodagu or- fall asleep. Selected survey uraŋguga/voraŋgiyadu/oragada/ora and contracted argu/ergu responses retain this sleep stem with ordinary elicitation endings and initial-vowel/glide notation. The Toda orkʰa response is excluded because its verbal versus nominal/causative interpretation remains unclear. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3754 gives Tamil nilavu/nilā, Malayalam nilāvu/lāvu, Kodagu nelaci, Telugu nela, Gadaba neliŋ and Gondi nalenj/nelenj/lēnj moon. Selected nilav/nelavu/lāvu/nelaci and nella/nelli survey responses are comparative variants retaining the moon sense and source consonant reductions; no Indo-Aryan candra forms are included. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4275 gives Tamil putu/putiya new, puttaṉ new person or thing, Malayalam puttan a new thing, Kota pud and Kodagu pudiyë new. Selected puttan/putuvan/putusu/pudiyai-type survey responses include the source’s nominalized person/thing forms and ordinary adjective endings; the original new gloss is retained. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3263(a) documents tiṉ/tinn- eat, with Tamil past tiṉṟ-, Kannada tind-, Kodagu timb-/tind-, Kota/Toda tiḏ- and Gadaba tin-/tiy-/tinḍ-. Selected simple and ordinary tense/nominal forms retain that eat stem and its documented alternants; survey endings, voicing and vowels are preserved. Longer auxiliary/pronoun clauses and uncertain rounded-vowel forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
